Triggers.value: The same time of day the event occurred
Beginning to feel detached or unreal

Maladaptive Strategies.value: I spend long hours on my phone, games, or internet to avoid thinking
I drink alcohol, take medication or use drugs
Watching TV programmes/ films or reading about similar events

Threat.value: Unexpected movement nearby causes me to react as if I am in danger
I react with alarm when someone touches me unexpectedly
I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger

Memory.value: I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind.
When I remember the event I feel intense guilt
I feel like I am only remembering parts of what happened and the rest is missing

Negative Appraisals.value: The event happened to me because of the sort of person I am
Somebody else would not have gotten into this situation

vignette: Kai had always been a man who liked his routine. As an electrician, he took pride in being on time and getting the job done efficiently. But all of that changed on a fateful evening two years ago when he was assaulted by a group of strangers while walking home from work. The event occurred at exactly 8:45 PM, and ever since then, Kai had found himself growing increasingly anxious as the clock approached that time every day. As the anniversary of the assault drew near, Kai began to feel detached and unreal, like he was observing his life from outside his body. He would catch himself zoning out in the middle of conversations or staring blankly at walls for minutes on end. It was as if his mind had developed a coping mechanism to deal with the trauma, but it only seemed to make things worse. To avoid these feelings, Kai started spending more and more time on his phone, playing games or scrolling through social media until the early hours of the morning. But even that couldn't block out the triggers that haunted him. Every time he heard a door slam shut or saw someone approaching him unexpectedly, Kai's heart would skip a beat. He would react with alarm, his senses on high alert as if he was still in danger. His partner had started to notice these episodes and tried to reassure him, but Kai couldn't shake off the feeling that he was constantly being watched. When memories of the assault flooded back, Kai felt like he was reliving it all over again. He remembered the sound of footsteps behind him, the feeling of fear as he realized he was being attacked. But there were gaps in his memory too - moments where everything went black and he couldn't recall what happened next. This incomplete picture only fueled his guilt and self-blame. Kai had come to believe that if only he had been more aware of his surroundings or reacted faster, the assault might not have happened. As these thoughts swirled in his head, Kai started to question his own character. He wondered if there was something fundamentally flawed about him that made him a target for violence. This sense of hopelessness crept into every aspect of his life, making him doubt his future and compare himself unfavorably to others. Why had he been so foolish as to walk alone at night? Why hadn't he fought back harder? Kai's negative appraisals fed back into his threat perception, making him even more vigilant and jumpy. He began avoiding unfamiliar places or situations where he might feel vulnerable, always scanning the surroundings for potential dangers. This hypervigilance only seemed to heighten his sense of anxiety, creating a vicious cycle that left Kai exhausted and drained. As the months went by, Kai's substance use increased too - a few drinks after work to calm his nerves or medication to help him sleep. He knew it wasn't healthy, but he felt like he had no other way to cope with the memories and emotions that haunted him. His partner tried to stage an intervention, but Kai pushed them away, convinced that they just didn't understand what he was going through. It was only when Kai's job began to suffer - missed deadlines, botched repairs - that he realized he needed help. He couldn't keep living in this state of constant fear and self-doubt. As he sat in the therapist's office for the first time, Kai felt a glimmer of hope that maybe, just maybe, he could break free from this cycle of trauma and start rebuilding his life. But as he looked back on the past two years, Kai couldn't shake off the fear that had taken hold of him. What if he never regained control over his memories? What if the triggers always stayed one step ahead of him? The uncertainty was suffocating, but for now, it was all Kai could do to take a tentative step forward and hope that someday, somehow, things would get better.
